result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A supplier registered without terms gets 30. All 610 tests pass offline, including a new `SupplierTest` case for the Swedish example (45 days, renegotiated to 14).

What changed:
- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is zero or more.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The old 5-argument constructor is kept and defaults to 30, so the ~80 existing call sites still compile.
- **`DataStore.java`**: create and update write the value. The four listings you named (by name, by country, by minimum rating, and single lookup by id) read it. The other supplier queries that build a `Supplier` (purchase suggestions, spending, performance, purchased quantity, supplier-per-category) also read it, so they don't silently show 30.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests, one for the renegotiation across all four listings and one for the 30-day default.

Two things to know:
- The 5-argument constructor silently sets terms to 30. Any future update that uses it will reset a renegotiated supplier's terms. I left it in place to keep the change small.
- I did not change `DemoScenario`. Its `main` method is at the JVM method-size limit, and one extra argument there broke compilation. The demo creates Nordic with the default, so its existing update call already keeps the same value.

Nothing is committed.
